maya (Support): raising from CS: customer ACME-42 (TKT-3827) reports rerank API started returning 400/500s for requests that include emojis and some legacy-encoded text. They see 'invalid UTF-8' / 'UnicodeDecodeError' in our logs. Can we triage?

jessica (CS): they said it started after upgrading their client lib to 2.3.4, but they repro with raw curl too. sending sample payload they used.

maya (Support): payload they sent (sanitized):
```json
{
  "query": "Sort these answers",
  "candidates": ["Hello\u0000World", "Résumé", "Emoji: \ud83d\ude0a", "Mojibake: Caf\xE9"]
}
```

diego (Eng Runtime): can you paste the exact error from the service logs? need the stack.

maya (Support): log excerpt:
```
2026-02-05T14:12:03Z ERROR rerank.service.RequestHandler - failed to parse request body
Traceback (most recent call last):
  File "/srv/re-ranker/rerank_input_validator.py", line 78, in validate
    body = raw_body.decode('utf-8')
UnicodeDecodeError: 'utf-8' codec can't decode byte 0x80 in position 27: invalid start byte
  File "/srv/re-ranker/rerank.py", line 212, in handle_request
    raise InvalidEncodingError("invalid utf8 in request body")
```

sam (Eng-ML): looks like raw bytes are making it to the service. two likely sources: client is sending text encoded in a non-UTF8 charset (windows-1252) or binary/null bytes are embedded (\u0000). The tokenizer and model pipeline assume valid UTF-8.

diego (Eng Runtime): agreed. quick repro I did locally (bash) - you can recreate with \x80:
```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood-inference.example.com/v1/rerank \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json; charset=utf-8" \
  -d $'{"query":"q","candidates":["Good","Bad\x80Byte"]}'
```
That produces the same decode error on our canary.

jessica (CS): customer wants workaround they can apply today. they can't change all clients at once. any short-term sanitization we can recommend?

sam (Eng-ML): temp workaround for them: sanitize on client before send. examples below. important: remove NULs and replace invalid sequences, normalize.
Python:
```py
s = original_str
# drop NULs
s = s.replace('\u0000', '')
# force encoding roundtrip, replace invalid bytes
safe = s.encode('utf-8', 'replace').decode('utf-8')
```
Node.js:
```js
let s = original;
// drop null bytes
s = s.replace(/\u0000/g, '');
// ensure string is valid UTF-8 when building buffers
const buf = Buffer.from(s, 'utf8');
const safe = buf.toString('utf8');
```

diego (Eng Runtime): server-side options: 1) return 400 with explicit message 'invalid utf-8 in request body; remove null bytes or send valid UTF-8' (better UX), or 2) auto-sanitize (strip NULs, replace invalid sequences with U+FFFD) and log counts. I prefer (2) as a short-term canary to reduce customer impact, but we must metric the rate and ensure we don't silently mask bugs.

maya (Support): customer ok with server-side sanitization as a temporary mitigation. they'd still like an explanation and a patch for their client later.

sam (Eng-ML): implementation note: sanitizer should run before tokenization and before hashing/signature checks. simple algo: try decode utf-8, on UnicodeDecodeError run 'lossy' decode and replace NULs with empty string. emit a header 'X-Rerank-Sanitized: 1' and count sanitized_request metric.

diego (Eng Runtime): I'll open a small PR to add sanitization + metric + clear 400 when the payload is >2% non-UTF8 in a request. will canary to 10% of traffic. rollback plan included.

ops-bot: @oncall has been paged for the canary deploy. :bell:

oncall: I'll watch error-rate dashboards. set alert: rerank.decode_errors > 1% over 5m -> page. will also look for spikes in sanitized_request metric.

jessica (CS): please share exact text we can send the customer for TKT-3827 with the quick client fixes and ETA for the server canary.

maya (Support): message to customer drafted: "We've identified invalid UTF-8 / null bytes in some requests. As a quick fix, sanitize strings on the client (examples attached). We're deploying a temporary server sanitizer to reduce failures for compatible requests; we will notify you when the canary is live. If you can share a minimal repro payload we can test on our side (TKT-3827), that'd be great." :thumbsup:

diego (Eng Runtime): assigned to me and sam. PR opened: https://git.redwood/eng/runtime/pulls/2456 (canary -> 10%). will post status here when deployed. :gear:

maya (Support): I'll update TKT-3827 with workaround instructions and will escalate to account team if they want a follow-up SDK patch. thanks all. :eyes:
